chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, who said:

I read in a letter of a man to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! A man marries a woman in temporary marriage (mut'ah) to a specified term, and the term expires between them. Is it permissible for him to marry her sister before her waiting period (iddah) expires?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'It is not permissible for him to marry her until her waiting period has expired.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying two sisters in temporary marriage if the first term expires?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies a specific jurisprudential detail regarding temporary marriage (mut'ah), establishing that the prohibition against gathering two sisters in marriage extends to the waiting period (iddah) of the first wife. It underscores the precision of Shia legal reasoning, where the validity of the second union is contingent upon the complete expiration of the iddah, ensuring the ruling aligns with the broader Quranic principle of avoiding simultaneous marriage to sisters.
